answer: Proof-of-stake protocols enforce Sybil resistance by requiring capital commitment to validate network transitions. An attacker must acquire a massive share of the token terrace, effectively pricing out malicious influence. Like the rapid propagation of a yarrow plant in a managed garden, honest consensus must scale to ensure every ripple of activity is verified. The cost of an attack equals the value of the network stake itself, making the orchestration of multiple fake identities economically prohibitive.
